prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were injured — that’s stressful. I can’t pick one single lawyer for you, but I can tell you exactly how to choose the right attorney in Pleasanton (Alameda County) and what to do next so you hire the best fit for your case.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical treatment now and keep all records and bills. Your health comes first and records are key evidence.
- Get the police report (Pleasanton PD or CHP if on a state highway). Note the report number and officer name.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene, skid marks, damage; witness names/phones; any video (dashcams, CCTV).
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without talking to a lawyer first.
- Keep a diary of symptoms, medical visits, missed work, and expenses.
- Be aware of the statute of limitations: typically 2 years from the injury date for personal injury claims in California (fewer for claims against a government entity — often 6 months to present a claim). Act promptly.

Which type of lawyer to look for
- A personal injury attorney who focuses on car-accident cases. If your injuries are catastrophic or it’s a wrongful death, look for attorneys who handle those specifically.
- Prefer firms with trial experience (many cases settle, but you want an attorney who will go to court if needed).
- Local experience in Alameda County / Pleasanton courts is a plus.

How to evaluate and choose (criteria)
- Experience with car-accident cases and similar injuries (e.g., whiplash, fractures, head trauma, spinal).
- Track record: settlements/verdicts, trial experience.
- Client reviews, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Google/Yelp) and disciplinary record (State Bar of California).
- Communication style and who will handle the work (lead attorney or mainly paralegals).
- Fee arrangement: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no recovery = no fee); typical contingency is about 33% for settlement before suit, often up to 40% if suit and/or appeal. Get the exact percentage and who pays costs/expenses if you lose.
- Availability and responsiveness — how often they’ll update you and preferred contact method.
- Comfort level and trust — you should feel confident they understand your goals.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? How many and with what results?
- Do you try cases or mainly settle?
- Who will handle my case day to day?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What’s a realistic timeline and likely value range for my case?
- Any conflicts of interest with involved insurers or parties?
- How often will you update me?

Local resources to find attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (referral to vetted attorneys).
- State Bar of California website to verify license status and discipline history.
- Online reviews (Google, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell) and local recommendations.
- Ask your primary care doctor or other lawyers you know for referrals.

What documents to bring to consultations
- Police report number/copy
- Photos of scene, vehicles, injuries
- Medical records and bills, ER notes
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s)
- Pay stubs for lost wages, employer notes
- Any correspondence from insurers
- Witness contact info

Practical expectations
- Most car-accident cases settle without trial, but cases with serious injuries or disputed fault may go to litigation.
- Typical timeline: months to a year+ depending on treatment completion and negotiation; complex cases can take longer.
- Don’t accept the insurer’s first settlement offer without legal advice — early offers are often low.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft a short message or script to contact attorneys.
- Provide a list of 5 attorneys in Pleasanton/Dublin/Hayward area (I’ll need your zip code and any preferences: severity of injury, willingness to go to trial, language needs). Note: I can’t fetch live web results, but I can recommend how to search and what to look for based on your criteria.

Tell me a bit more (severity of injury, any fault dispute, whether you’ve talked to your insurer) and I’ll help you narrow down what to ask and how to pick the best lawyer for your case.
